title: Tiered defer-shed and connection latch repair
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We observed a class of incidents where short-lived regional egress spikes combined with aggressive connection reopen logic caused repeated tenant circuit flips and unnecessary evictions. This PR introduces a conservative, tiered 'defer-shed' mechanism that delays hard egress shedding for recently warmed connections and adds a connection latch that prevents rapid open/close cycles from retriggering circuit state transitions. Changes include runtime logic, new telemetry, tests, and a small CLI to toggle the defer tier for canaries. Checklist: 1) Add tiered defer-shed policy and config knobs; 2) Implement connection latch with epoch-backed cooldown; 3) Wire telemetry for shed/latched events and expose two histograms; 4) Add unit and integration tests; 5) Run directed load tests and smoke on staging; 6) Prepare release notes and roll-out plan. Impact: aims to reduce churn in regional failovers and avoid cascading tenant evictions during transient hotspots. Rollout: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with metric thresholds and automatic rollback on increased eviction rate. Related: ENG-1987 tracks follow-ups for per-tenant tuning and Console flags.

release_notes: Introduce 'defer-shed' tier that delays hard egress shedding for recently warmed connections to reduce tenant eviction churn during transient spikes.
Add connection latch to prevent rapid open/close cycles from retriggering circuit transitions and causing oscillation.
Config knobs: runtime.defer_shed.enabled, runtime.defer_shed.cooldown_ms, runtime.connection_latch.window_epochs. Rollout controlled via canary_ctl.
No breaking changes expected. Backfill: operators should monitor eviction rate and shed_deferred_total during rollout.
